title: Nemi Mang Phura
identifier_type: Project identifier, not an archival shelfmark
credits: Original analytical source: translated into Shan by Chaichuen Khamdaengyodtai, rendered into English by Stephen Morey, then jointly revised. Manuscript belonging to Sri Gileswar Bailung Phukon, Bokota; photographed December 2008. The modern English readings follow the supplied digital edition.
scope: All 1,653 numbered entries of the supplied edition are retained. Ahom continuation rows and omitted legacy glyphs are restored from the numbered analytical source. Entry 1653 has no recoverable Ahom text and retains its damaged-text notice.
notes: The old 333-page edition contained 46,606 PUA characters in 40 distinct codes. The 40 embedded glyphs match those independently verified in Ming Mvng Lung Phai.

The old edition frequently retained only the first Ahom row of a passage and omitted additional glyphs. The source master now includes every Ahom continuation row before the primary translation. The earlier text is retained in the audit for comparison.

For example, passage 2 restores the final words for the renowned realm; passage 1652 restores the final words and section mark. English wording is unchanged. Source page references allow every passage to be checked.

No new translation is claimed. The analytical source and original manuscript are separate records, and the source may itself contain uncertain readings. Repeated signs, detached marks, and source gap markers are preserved.
translation_basis: The existing modern English edition is preserved verbatim, apart from layout whitespace. Its 21 uncertain-reading labels and six damaged-text notices remain.
folio_mapping: Not supplied at record level. Analytical-source page numbers are not manuscript folios.

An unidentified legacy slot P (0x50) is represented as [unresolved-50] in five passages. The available legacy font contains a missing-glyph box in this slot. The surrounding transcription does not establish a unique Unicode identity, so no replacement is guessed. Entries 120 and 265 have no independent English sentence; the source continues their translations in the following entries.

title: Bar Amra
identifier_type: Project identifier for the working witness
credits: Inherited readings from the Ahom Dictionary Resource Project and manuscript-referenced SEAlang dictionary supplements; Zeenat Tabassum and Stephen Morey (2010) for two additions.
scope: 1,236 recovered records aligned to 61 supplied images. Four whole folios remain untranscribed; 55 numbered IDs lack accepted readings. No complete entry has confidence A.
notes: Tai-Ahom headwords and Assamese explanations written in Ahom script are separate language fields.
The four A-rated headwords do not certify their entire entries.
Image sequence is not a folio number. EAP373/26/2 canvas 3 matches 1r; canvas 21 matches 10r. No replacement for 26r/26v was established.
translation_basis: Inherited English lexical glosses; unresolved senses remain unresolved.
folio_mapping: Explicit folio, image and facsimile-page mappings preserved from the revised source register.
